title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 593-596): Grothendieck is computing the group law in a group of triples x = (u, a, b), or equivalently (u, α, β). These come from solutions of 'loop equations' in a fundamental-group setting indexed by (ρ, σ). Here u acts by automorphisms, τ and τ' are distinguished involutions, and ε_2, ε_3 = ε_3(χ(u)) are ±1-valued characters. By (61), a = ε_3(τ') α^{-1} u, where ε_3(τ') equals 1 or τ' according to the sign ε_3; the same holds for the primed and double-primed elements. For a product x'' = x' x one has ε_3'' = ε_3 ε_3' and a'' = ε a' a, with the sign ε ∈ {±1} given by (63).

On the previous page Grothendieck first guessed, 'by symmetry', that α'' = ε u'(α) α'. Checking it, he found this holds only if [ε_3(τ'), a'] = 1, which is a 'draconian' restriction when ε_3 = -1. He then derived the correct formula with a commutator correction term.

This page rewrites that formula. Since ε'_3(τ') a' = α'^{-1} u' (because τ' is an involution), one gets (65): α'' = (ε u'(α) α') · [α'^{-1} u', ε_3(τ')]. Grothendieck calls this 'un peu abracadabrante', and a marginal note says this monster cost him much trouble.

Next he turns to a structural question. The group S_0^Π Γ^!_{ρ,σ} is a central extension of Z^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ U^![σ] by μ = {±1}. Is this extension trivial, given that its restrictions to the subgroups Z^!' and Z^!''' are trivial? He takes the inverse images S_0^Π Γ^!' and S_0^Π Γ^!''' as intersections (66). These give central extensions (67), which split via the subgroups S_0^{Π_0} Γ^!' and S_0^{Π_0} Γ^!'''. Hence the products (68): S_0^Π Γ^!' ≅ S_0^{Π_0} Γ^!' × μ, and likewise for the triple-primed group.

The next page asks whether these splitting subgroups are normal in the whole group. If so, the extension would descend to extensions of the quotients Z^!/Z^!' ≅ ±1 and Z^!/Z^!''' ≅ ±1 by μ. He then tests normality using the explicit element x = (τ, τ', τ). This is elementary group cohomology: a class in H^2(Z, μ) that vanishes on two index-2 subgroups.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The formula (65) agrees with the corrected formula at the end of the previous page. Because τ' is an involution, [ε'_3(τ') a', ε_3(τ')] equals [ε'_3(τ')(a'), ε_3(τ')], whether ε'_3(τ') acts by conjugation or by left multiplication.
In (66) the first line uses the label Γ^!'; the text just above writes 'S_0^Π U^!'''' for the second group, an evident slip of notation (U for Γ).

ideas.what: Explicit group law (composition of triples) for symmetries of solutions of the loop equations, including a commutator correction term in α''.
ideas.modern_name: Twisted semidirect-product law, analogous to the composition law of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (λ, f) acting on (x, y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for variants
ideas.where_published: Not published; the 'Longue Marche' (1981) contains related but different computations

ideas.what: Deciding whether a central extension by μ = {±1} is trivial, knowing it splits over two index-2 subgroups; reduction to normality of the splitting complements.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of H^2(G, Z/2) classes to subgroups; inflation from quotients

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but laborious working computation: a group law with a correction term, and a check of whether a central extension by ±1 splits. The personal marginal remark about the 'monster' formula is of biographical interest only. Nothing indicates a result or connection absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'ε'_3(τ')a' = α'^{-1}u'' with lowercase a' (not α'), matching (61) on the previous page and the underbrace in (65).
The underbrace in (65) reads 'ε'_3(τ')a''; it labels α'^{-1}u'.
The sign ε in (65) is 'défini dans (63)'; the fraction-like symbol Π/Δ_ρ (with Δ crossed out) is a separate marginal annotation.
The marginal note is roughly: 'Sic! Voilà le monstre qui m'a fait passer par des [sueurs froides?] ... un véritable exercice de patience!' — the reading is uncertain.
In the 'Soient ...' line the second group is written S_0^Π Γ^!''' (the machine transcription has U^!''', which matches a slip in the text but not (66)).
